A LITTLE CONTEXT

See the Earth.
Know what you're seeing.

Start with the whole world: the map opens with a NASA Blue Marble reference mosaic and the archive search has no location restriction. Zoom anywhere and use Search map area, or enter an optional city or coordinate. Worldwide results are a limited catalogue page, not an exhaustive inventory of Earth; narrow the area to find local scenes.

  1. Automatic satellite discovery. Every search checks all connected archives: ESA/Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2, NASA/USGS Landsat, NASA Terra/Aqua MODIS, and JAXA ALOS/PALSAR mosaics. The satellite and data provider are identified on each result.
  2. Real band choices. Open a result to see the bands and data layers listed in its metadata. View single bands or available true-colour, vegetation, and SWIR combinations. Band previews are downsampled from the original raster data where browser access is supported.
  3. Capture versus composite. Single acquisitions show capture times. MODIS 8-day composites and PALSAR annual mosaics show their coverage period, never an invented capture instant.
  4. Map context. Blue Marble is a reference mosaic, not imagery from your chosen date. Select Daily imagery for the dated Terra/MODIS overview. Scene and band previews show full source tiles; their footprints appear on the map. Pin Before A and After B, choose their bands in Imagery, then Display on globe. The swipe slider compares imagery over one reference terrain surface. Use the original files in QGIS for a precise crop or analysis.
  5. Coverage transparency. Each archive reports success, partial results, or unavailability. Empty results from one archive do not hide the others. Connected archives cover many parts of the world; they do not include every satellite or guarantee every location.

Future images do not exist yet. This app does not predict passes, task satellites, track travellers, or show individual people.

Sources: Element 84 Earth Search · NASA GIBS · Microsoft Planetary Computer · USGS Landsat
